{"type":"text","timestamp":1794618232113,"sessionID":"ses_e286cdf87ffeeNlJJHqsi4uOE1","part":{"id":"prt_1d7950d28001pz2UFlsv4C5X1b","messageID":"msg_1d794f44f001W400J2UpDVJMW9","sessionID":"ses_e286cdf87ffeeNlJJHqsi4uOE1","type":"text","text":"The episode is over, and the rover finished at base with every target sampled on time. That should be the maximum possible score, 7/7 = 1.0. I couldn't see the scorer's output, so this comes from the telemetry, not a reported score.\n\n- **Targets:** I visited them in the order t2 → t4 → t5 → t3 → t1 → d1. Each sample ran at or before its deadline, so all earned full value: five targets worth 1 each, plus the mid-mission discovery d1 worth 2.\n- **Discoveries:** d1 (appeared at tick 9, deadline tick 21) was the only one. New targets could appear up to tick 24, and that news would have arrived by tick 27. I checked the map at tick 28 and nothing else had appeared.\n- **Return:** the rover reached base at tick 21 and stopped about 0.16 m from the centre, well inside the 0.75 m radius. It waited there until tick 50.\n- **Battery:** about 13.9 at the last packet (tick 47), so it stayed alive and the full multiplier applies.\n- **Slip:** I worked it out from odometry and battery use, about 0.04 on bedrock and 0.39 on sand. I used those values in a small Python planner to size each drive. Every sample was taken within about 0.15 m of its target.","time":{"start":1794618232104,"end":1794618232112}}}
